sections.title: Transmission Network & Regulatory KPIs
sections.subtitle: The physical asset base behind the regulated revenue, and the CERC tariff-incentive metric it earns on.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Power Grid Corporation of India Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Power Grid Corporation of India Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Power Grid Corporation of India Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Power Grid Corporation of India Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Power Grid Corporation of India Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Power Grid Corporation of India Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Power Grid Corporation of India Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Power Grid Corporation of India Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

networkScale.title: Transmission line length and transformation capacity
networkScale.content:
Transmission line length (circuit km) and transformation capacity (MVA) are the two physical measures of the regulated asset base Power Grid is allowed to earn a return on.

For Power Grid Corporation of India Limited: under CERC's cost-of-service tariff regulations, revenue tracks the capitalised asset base, not a sales volume -- so this chart is closer to the company's real growth driver than the headline revenue line, which only recognises capacity after a project is commissioned (CERC's "deemed date of commercial operation").

What to watch:

  • Capacity additions slowing while committed capex (TBCB wins, inter-state transmission schemes) stays large -- a sign of execution delay, not demand
  • Transformation capacity (MVA) growing faster than line length -- more substations/upgrades per km of new line

substations.title: Substations
substations.content:
The count of grid substations Power Grid owns and operates, the discrete nodes that step voltage up or down across the interstate transmission network.

For Power Grid Corporation of India Limited: each new substation is a commissioned project entering the regulated asset base; the pace of additions is the clearest read on how fast approved capex (inter-state transmission system schemes won via tariff-based competitive bidding or awarded on a cost-plus basis) is converting into revenue-earning assets.

What to watch:

  • Additions bunching late in a fiscal year (project commissioning near year-end is common in Indian infrastructure)
  • Count growing while transmission line length is flat -- substation upgrades rather than network expansion

systemAvailability.title: System availability
systemAvailability.content:
System availability is the percentage of time a transmission asset is available for service, averaged across the network. It is disclosed quarterly/annually and reported only where the company has broken it out.

For Power Grid Corporation of India Limited: this is the single KPI CERC's transmission tariff regulations price directly. Availability above the CERC normative threshold earns an incentive on top of the allowed return; availability below it draws a disincentive that cuts straight into regulated revenue. Power Grid has run at roughly 99.8%, comfortably above norm, for most of the last decade -- so the chart is really a check for an unusual dip (storm damage, grid disturbance, fire) rather than a trend to extrapolate.

What to watch:

  • Any single-period drop of more than a few tenths of a point -- it converts directly into a tariff disincentive that quarter
  • Whether a dip coincides with a named outage (cyclone, forest fire, grid-code disturbance) disclosed in the filing, versus a reporting change

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Power Grid Corporation of India Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Power Grid Corporation of India Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
